Hi Stephanie / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving Lumina’s procurement review forward and have two immediate asks before our security committee meets next Thursday: 1) a short onboarding checklist that maps to our PHI ingestion flows, and 2) confirmation on a few potential BAA exceptions related to analytics exports to our downstream vendor.

Specifically:
- Can you provide a one-page onboarding checklist showing steps, data flows, and expected timelines for PHI onboarding?
- Our analytics vendor will receive de-identified event data for product analytics. We need to know whether Redwood considers that a subprocessor event that requires contract-level approval, and if so what controls you impose (e.g., hashing, tokenization, contractual restrictions).
- We also want a high-level note on key management (customer-managed keys vs. Redwood KMS) and where egress occurs (US-only or multi-region).

If you can send the checklist and a draft BAA redline we’ll share both with our counsel (copied). Also please call out any operational exceptions (SLA, retention, or audit log access) we should expect.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our timeline is to lock procurement items by Friday 8/20.

Alex —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a concise onboarding checklist and our standard BAA with a few clauses we typically expect to discuss. Short answers below, and Rishi is copied for the technical details.

Quick answers:
- Onboarding checklist attached: "Lumina_HIPAA_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx" (timeline, owners, required documents).
- Analytics exports: Redwood treats downstream analytics vendors as subprocessors. We allow controlled exports under contract with the following options: hashed/pseudonymized exports, contractual restrictions on re-identification, or a dedicated isolated export pipeline by request.
- KMS: default is Redwood-managed KMS (AES-256 at rest). We support customer-managed keys (CMK) for Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted customers we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key via our KMS integrations subject to audit and key-rotation windows.
- Data egress: by default host-region (US regions available); we can commit US-only residency in contract for enterprise plans.

Attachments (stubs):
- Lumina_HIPAA_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx (Excel, 14KB)
- BAA_Draft_Redline.docx (Word, 28KB)

Stephanie / Alex —

I reviewed the BAA draft at a high level. Two items Lumina counsel will want clarified or tightened before we can sign:

1) Subprocessing: the BAA should require Redwood to obtain written consent for any subprocessor that will receive PHI beyond aggregated telemetry (we may accept limited analytics exports if the data is de-identified under the HIPAA expert determination standard). Please confirm whether Redwood will accept a clause that requires prior written approval for any subprocessor with PHI access.

2) KMS / Key ownership & access: Lumina is requesting a stronger commitment around key custody for PHI stored at rest. If Redwood can offer customer-managed keys (CMK) in your Dedicated or Private options, that would be acceptable; for Hosted we need extra contractual controls and monthly key rotation documentation.

Also: please provide SOC 2 Type II report link and a short network diagram showing the egress path to third-party analytics vendors.

If you can send those items and a redline with proposed language for subprocessor consent, we’ll review and aim to return a clean signable BAA by 8/20.

Regards,

Miles / Alex —

Following up with the technical details you requested. Summary first, then specifics.

Summary:
- Subprocessor model: Redwood maintains a subprocessors registry. For PHI we treat any downstream party that receives identifiable PHI as a subprocessor requiring contract-level controls. We are open to a clause requiring written consent for new PHI subprocessors; standard large-enterprise approach is an approved-subprocessor list plus notice and an approval window. We can accept a requirement for prior written approval on a case-by-case basis (preferably limited to vendors receiving identifiable PHI).
- De-identification approach: for analytics exports we support a pipeline that performs irreversible hashing + salt per customer plus suppression of direct identifiers. If Lumina needs HIPAA expert-determination level de-identification we can work with your privacy team to provide deterministic proofs and transformation logs.
- KMS & keys: Hosted: Redwood-managed KMS (HSM-backed) with tenant isolation and auditable key access logs; we provide key-rotation reports on request. Dedicated/Private: full CMK support with customer KMS integration (cloud KMS or on-prem HSM).
- Data residency & egress: default US regions only for this proposal; egress to analytics vendors can be restricted to a dedicated export pipeline terminated in a Redwood-controlled intermediate account with ACLs that prevent re-identification.

Operational notes (short):
- Retention: default retention configurable from 30 days to 7 years; we can set a contractual retention schedule for PHI.
- Audit logs: we provide per-request audit events (user, call, model, tokens) retained per contract and can provide periodic extracts for audits.

I’ve attached our network diagram showing the export flow (network_diagram_v2.pdf). For your proposed subprocessor consent language, here’s a suggested snippet you can use in the BAA redline: 

"Redwood shall not engage any subprocessor to process PHI without prior written consent from Customer for subprocessors that will receive identifiable PHI. For non-identifiable telemetry or aggregated analytics, Redwood may use pre-approved subprocessors and will provide notice 30 days prior to any change."

If that aligns we’ll incorporate into the BAA and return a redline. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
